method: Direct visual and textual inspection of ten consecutive item bodies in the user-supplied Kehot publisher scan. OCR was a navigation aid only; the scan pages were rendered and checked, and no blocked crawler was used.
identity_relation: All ten letters were existing locator-only bibliographic identities and were enriched in place from their inspected bodies. The index form ד׳תקם is preserved for the letter commonly rendered numerically as 560.

evidence_family_dedup.counting_rule: Distinct correspondence items about one emissary journey; they are not counted as independent proof of the journey's effects.
The two letters are distinct documents in one controversy and substantially cross-reference the same technical-halakhic argument; they are not independent corroboration for repeated claims.
A distinct response sharing the same prayer-rite doctrine family; repeated doctrine is synthesized without multiplying independent authority.
The Hebrew propositions are a research translation of the Yiddish item and not a second witness.

verification_scope: Ten letter bodies were inspected across PDF pages 323-338. Incoming correspondence, cited works, telegrams, engineering evidence, institutional and medical files, financial records and later outcomes were not independently inspected.
rights_note: Only bounded non-verbatim research paraphrases and locators were recorded; no protected letter was copied in full.
quality_note: All propositions are source-grounded paraphrases. Secretary signatures, fragments, historical technical scope, medical and halakhic limitations, Yiddish translation status and Evidence Family links are preserved.
